title: Normal residue extension and surjective decomposition action
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, and residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $L/K$ be a finite normal separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], where normal means that the minimal polynomial of every element over $K$ splits into linear factors over $L$. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], let $\mathfrak n$ be a maximal ideal of $B$, and put $E=B/\mathfrak n$ with its induced $k$-algebra structure. Define $D=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(L):\sigma(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak n\}$. Then $E/k$ is normal: for every $x\in E$, its minimal polynomial over $k$ splits into linear factors over $E$. The residue-action homomorphism $\rho:D\to\operatorname{Aut}_k(E)$, defined by $\rho(\sigma)(\bar b)=\overline{\sigma(b)}$, is surjective. No separability of $E/k$ is required.

source.place: Tag 09ED (lemma-galois-galois), assertions (1)-(2); their proof uses A=B^G and lemma-one-orbit-geometric.

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is a principal ideal domain. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $A$ integrally closed in its fraction field $K$. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$. The finite normal separable extension $L/K$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]; thus $G$ is finite and $L^G=K$. These are the two inputs in the first sentence of the proof of Stacks 09ED.

source.place: Tag 09ED (lemma-galois-galois), proof of (1)-(2): A=B^G and the application of Tag 0BRJ (lemma-one-orbit-geometric).

proof.text: The integral closure $B$ is a subring of $L$ containing $A$, by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. If $b\in B$ satisfies a monic equation with coefficients in $A$, then applying $\sigma\in G$ to that equation gives the same monic equation for $\sigma(b)$, since $\sigma$ fixes $K$ and therefore $A$. Thus $\sigma(B)\subseteq B$; applying this to $\sigma^{-1}$ gives equality. Restriction therefore defines an action of $G$ on $B$ by ring automorphisms fixing $A$ pointwise. Restriction preserves the identity and composition: for $b\in B$, $1(b)=b$ and $(\sigma\tau)|_B(b)=\sigma|_B(\tau|_B(b))$. Thus the restrictions satisfy the group action laws.

source.place: Tag 09ED (lemma-galois-galois), proof of (1)-(2): A=B^G and the application of Tag 0BRJ (lemma-one-orbit-geometric).

proof.text: Every element of $A$ is fixed. Conversely, if $b\in B$ is fixed by all of $G$, then [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] gives $b\in K$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] it is integral over $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] gives $b\in A$. Consequently $B^G=A$, as an equality of subrings inside $L$, not just an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09ED (lemma-galois-galois), proof of (1)-(2): A=B^G and the application of Tag 0BRJ (lemma-one-orbit-geometric).

proof.text: Every element of $B$ is integral over $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical] with the zero ideal of $A$ (which is contained in its Jacobson radical): its maximal-preimage clause says that $\mathfrak n\cap A$ is maximal. As $A$ is local by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], this preimage is its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $\mathfrak n$ lies over $\mathfrak m_A$, and both are maximal, precisely the hypotheses on ideals needed in the quotient theorem.

source.place: Tag 09ED (lemma-galois-galois), proof of (1)-(2): A=B^G and the application of Tag 0BRJ (lemma-one-orbit-geometric).

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-finite-invariant-quotient-normal-action] with $R=A$, $S=B$, $H=G$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak n$. Steps 1-3 supply finiteness of $G$, its action fixing $A$, and $A=B^G$; step 4 supplies the maximal-ideal contraction. Its quotient fields are literally $F=A/\mathfrak m_A=k$ and $E=B/\mathfrak n$. Its subgroup $D_H(\mathfrak q)$ is exactly $D$ in the item, and its homomorphism sends the class of $b$ to the class of $\sigma(b)$, exactly $\rho$. The normality clause gives the required splitting for every $x\in E$, and the surjectivity clause lifts every $k$-automorphism of $E$ to $D$. The cited theorem requires no separability of $E/k$.
